uncertainty_type: Assumption sensitivity, NOT a confidence or identification interval

turnout_temporal_diagnostics.scope: Retrospective prediction in the surviving current-registration panel, not independent 2026 validation
turnout_temporal_diagnostics.known_total_conditioning_note: Uses only the observed overall 2022 participation total; matching that total is a constraint, not independent calibration evidence

normalization: Exact five-component Shapley attribution of two-party margin; signed percentages, suppressed below 1 pp net swing
limitations: Neither the registered-population model nor its latent transitions are observed 2026 individual histories.
Late participation is modeled from retrospective historical midterms and raked to provisional all-mode ballots.
Current registration predates Election Day; neither absence nor REMOVED proves an eligibility/residence exit.
Unmatched 2024 NC history includes unresolved interstate participants; the mover fraction is an assumption.
Conditional independence of turnout and prior choice within administrative cells is unvalidated.
Known prior votes outside Wake enter the geographic component, not new nationwide voters.
Voters under 18 throughout 2024 enter the eligibility component, never the prior-eligible-nonvoter component.
The historical choice model is calibrated to county 2024 totals; that is not independent validation.
A common choice-tilt calibrates entropy-regularized transitions to 2026 totals; aggregate fit cannot validate switching.
Contest abstention is assumed uniform within each year; other choices and contest effects stay separate.
Cohort and results snapshots have different clocks; accepted membership is a modeling constraint, not a proven counted-cohort match.
Administrative gender is not survey gender; it is an output partition, not a survey-gender predictor.
Education, income and residence-type estimates are unavailable in these administrative inputs.
Small joint cells and person-level scores are not included in the exported model results.
No nationwide transition estimate follows from this county pilot.

Demographic participation and prior-choice flows are conditional model counts using current administrative attributes and age in 2024, not observed fixed-attribute historical cohorts or eligible-population turnout rates.

selection_provenance.scope: Selection preserves every broad result/scenario exactly; private fine cells and unselected diagnostic groups excluded.

source_qualification.selection_basis: Broad native demographic categories selected after fitting for source support, descriptive relevance and disclosure protection, not estimated electoral outcomes. Selected rows are not exhaustive partitions. Multiple omitted race categories prevent recovering a small category by subtraction.
source_qualification.estimand: Assumption-conditioned transitions between actual 2024 Wake participation and a modeled 2026 electorate constrained to the frozen provisional county ballot total. Candidate choice and nonvoting transitions are latent, not individual observations.
source_qualification.historical_attributes: Age is assigned to 2024; other attributes are current administrative fields. These are not observed fixed-attribute historical demographic cohorts. Race and Hispanic ethnicity are separate native dimensions. Administrative gender is not survey gender.
source_qualification.population: The privately linked registration/baseline pool is not an eligible-population denominator. Unmatched history does not prove national nonparticipation; registration dates do not identify first-time voters. Known prior participants elsewhere enter a geographic component.
source_qualification.membership: Accepted early/mail membership is a modeling constraint, not proof of a matching counted cohort. Absence from this cohort is not absence from Election Day voting. Registration, history, accepted records and provisional results have different clocks.
source_qualification.model: Retrospective turnout probabilities and historical survey choice models are calibrated to county totals. Common choice tilts and conditional independence within cells are assumptions. Calibration to observed totals cannot validate latent switching or subgroup estimates.
source_qualification.diagnostics: Raw retrospective 2022 turnout calibration error is +9.738990186804353 percentage points. Even after conditioning on the known 2022 total, absolute subgroup error reaches 8.835569485825413 points for groups of at least 100. Brier improvement and arithmetic recovery do not validate individual transitions.
source_qualification.uncertainty: All 86 tested scenarios and marginal extrema are retained. Ranges vary loyalty, exit fractions, partisan late-turnout odds, unresolved movers, historical choice models and missing ethnicity. They are assumption sensitivity, not confidence intervals, identification bounds or exhaustive empirical uncertainty. Endpoints are not additive.
source_qualification.limits: Modeled nonvoting is separated from modeled eligibility/residence exit and contest blanks/other votes. Source missingness, survivor selection, migration, mortality, timing, recall, choice-model error and changing attributes remain. These results do not identify causal campaign persuasion, state totals or precinct transitions.
source_qualification.reproduction: All selected broad outputs for every scenario, fitted coefficients, complete public candidate/participation inputs, source receipts, model/linkage code and tests are included. Offline public reproduction verifies selected accounting and regenerates summaries and the archive. A fresh latent fit requires the deliberately excluded private native records and fine joint cells; the public package does not independently refit or identify them.
source_qualification.attribution: North Carolina State Board of Elections administrative participation/results and CES 2024 release 9, DOI 10.7910/DVN/X11EP6, CC0 historical survey models. Analysis is not endorsed by the data providers.
